fields.description:
## Context / Problem

`capabilities.py:330` defines a SINGLE global constant

    CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS = 4096

commented as the Opus floor, and applies it to every model. Anthropic's minimum cacheable prefix is
MODEL-DEPENDENT, and two independent investigations in this epic measured real floors that the
constant misdescribes.

## Measured evidence — two agents, two paths, neither trusting the other

MEASUREMENT A (via the overlap-judge path, `anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6`), bracketed two ways:
    bare API            922 tok -> no cache      1042 tok -> write 1035, read 1035
    real judge request  875 tok -> nothing       1250 tok -> write 1243, read 1243
  => sonnet-4-6 floor is ~1024, NOT 4096.

MEASUREMENT B (via a wrapped httpx transport, live A/B with identical marker and payload):
    haiku-4-5   1193 tok -> not cached
    haiku-4-5   2748 tok -> not cached
    haiku-4-5   4749 tok -> CACHED (w=4742 r=4742)
    sonnet-4-5   253 tok -> not cached
    sonnet-4-5  7930 tok -> CACHED (w=7923)
  => haiku-4-5's floor lies between 2748 and 4749; the sonnet-4-5 bracket is consistent with ~1024.

The two are not in conflict: they show the floor VARIES BY MODEL, which is exactly what a single
global constant cannot express. A floor of 4096 is roughly right for haiku and roughly 4x too high
for sonnet.

## Two distinct harms, both observed

1. FALSE NEGATIVE IN THE WARNING. `CACHE_MIN_PREFIX_TOKENS` gates `warn_if_cache_ineffective`
   (`structured_run.py:417-422`). A genuine caching failure on a sonnet call site with a 900-3000
   token prefix is silently below the global floor and never warns — the exact blind spot bug 7a79
   introduced the floor to avoid over-warning about, now over-corrected in the other direction.
2. IT MISLEADS SIZING DECISIONS. Work on ticket 8415 hoisted a shared prefix to make it cacheable and
   landed at 846 tokens. Against the real 1024 floor that is a near miss (+5.8% input tokens, zero
   cache); against the documented 4096 it looks hopeless. The constant materially changes what an
   engineer concludes is worth doing.

## A second, separable defect in the same predicate

`warn_if_cache_ineffective` compares total `input_tokens` against the floor, but what governs caching
is the size of the MARKED PREFIX, not the total request. A call with a 150-token marked prefix and a
7000-token unmarked user message clears the floor on totals and is uncacheable in fact. Bug f81d
carries the detail; noted here because any fix to the constant should fix the compared quantity too,
or the floor will still be measured against the wrong number.

## What is NOT established

The exact floor per model, from a documented source rather than bracketing. The measurements above are
empirical brackets on three models on one date; Anthropic publishes per-model minimums and those
should be the source of truth, with the measurements used to VERIFY rather than to define.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] The cache floor is model-dependent rather than one global constant, sourced from documented
      per-model minimums and carried on the capability record alongside `prompt_cache_style`.
- [x] `warn_if_cache_ineffective` compares the MARKED PREFIX size against that model's floor, not the
      total `input_tokens`.
- [x] A test pins that a sub-floor prefix on a LOW-floor model (sonnet) now warns where it previously
      did not, and fails before the fix.
- [x] A test pins that the haiku floor is not lowered to sonnet's, so the fix does not reintroduce the
      over-warning bug 7a79 removed.
- [x] make lint and make typecheck pass by exit code; the default selection is green.
